title: Our Uluru Games
subtitle: And now, we are both host and participant.

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: So, you're going to join them?!

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: I ... You know me. I'll always jump brim first into the unknown.

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: But the Foundation's already pulled their funding. The workers are already awaiting their reimbursement, and some players have already left ... How could we possibly hold a—

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: Mate, listen up.
There is an unfamiliar tension in the office. This may be the first real disagreement between the two old friends.

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: Those officers from the headquarters didn't give a damn whether the qualifiers were held or not. You could see it all over their faces.

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: All they wanted was to minimize their trouble. Did you see how quickly they applied for the cancelation and reimbursement? How hastily they made promises to pacify the people? I've never seen anyone more ready to get things over with.

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: Their job was done as soon as they got the player list. They'd probably already moved their attention to the qualifiers in other regions.

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: After all, our qualifiers are no different from the others to them, but ...

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: It means something to us, doesn't it? At least for me. This could be my chance to go to Australia. My very nature wants me to run free on the red land, to holler out and forget all my troubles.

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: I think that's what we all want.

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: In the heat of competition, people are at their best, their most pure.

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: Think about it, mate. You're not the only one who's put a lot of effort into this machine. It hurts me to see it rotting in the office, too.

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: If you're really going to give up because of a few words from an authority, then as your partner, I have to tell you:

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: Don't ever let anyone deny your achievements! Including yourself!
These words hit like a bomb, bringing his grand speech to an end.

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: Alright, calm down, old chap.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: Mr. Fog, the people want the qualifiers because they're for everyone.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: They provide each and every person with an equal opportunity to shine.
Sensing Mr. Fog's uncertainty, Tooth Fairy smiles as she offers her contribution.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: And that includes you and me. Although, for us, it'll be more like a battle to fight.
She gazes out the window at the people below, her head shaking gently in quiet frustration.
Words lodge in his throat like a date pit, neither going down nor coming up. After a pause, he sighs deeply.

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: Honestly, will these people stop sending me petitions?! I've been absolutely inundated with them!
Circling to the back of the desk, he opens a drawer and throws a pile of envelopes onto the desk with feigned anger.
Brimley and Tooth Fairy remain silent, unsure of how to interpret his intent.

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: *sigh* Fine. Someone has to keep everyone healthy. I'll do everything I can to minimize the damage from the smog.
After a moment, Mr. Fog lifts his head.

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: Don't worry. I'll talk to the Relief Centre to sort out all the paperwork for the event.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Here you are. This is yours. Please come here for a copy of the emergency guidebook if you don't have one! Make sure you read it carefully. We don't want anyone hurt if there's an emergency.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: And here, take this special sheet I enchanted to protect you from the smog. I came up with the idea a couple days ago.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: It can drive away the smog around you by controllin' the wind. Not very effective, but it's better than nothin'.

items.speaker: Worker I
items.text: Blimey, you did all this yourself?

items.speaker: Worker II
items.text: Cheers, little knocker-upper, but you don't need to worry about us. We've lived in the smog for generations. What can it hurt to hold a little sportin' event in it?

items.speaker: Will
items.text: Agreed. We asked for the exhibition ourselves, so we'll pay the price if anythin' happens.

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: Here's the confirmation of your application. Your contingency plan has been approved by the Relief Centre. My colleagues and I will do everything we can to keep you all safe.

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: As for the London Air Pollution Auto-Detecting Purifier MK. III, I'll do my best to fix it.

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: Next, we'll gather the athletes who have yet to leave the city and hold a small exhibition game.

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: Of course, it won't be an official event, but at least it'll give an opportunity for the athletes to demonstrate their hard work to a group of spectators.

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: I'm sure they'll be a great source of inspiration for the people of London as they cheer on their favorite athletes!

items.speaker: Will
items.text: Oi, Mr. Fog! I brought you this. It's Mrs. Brown's leek and potato soup with bread and butter.

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: Oh, Mrs. Brown. Please give her my thanks. Has everyone eaten?

items.speaker: Will
items.text: Yeah. Mrs. Brown, Mrs. Jones, Ben's son, and I have been cooking since four in the mornin' to get food out to everyone.

items.speaker: Will
items.text: But it still ain't enough. Almost everyone in the neighborhood's coming. Alright, I have to go make more soup. See you later!

items.speaker: Worker II
items.text: Hey, what's that you got from the knocker-upper?

items.speaker: Worker III
items.text: An enchanted sheet, apparently. She told me to blow it when I need to use it.

items.speaker: Worker II
items.text: *blow*

items.speaker: Worker II
items.text: Would you look at that? It conjured a gust of wind! We can use this while we're workin'.

items.speaker: Worker III
items.text: Yeah, it blows the smog away. Alright, well, sort of.

items.speaker: Little Lisa
items.text: Mr. Fog, Mr. Fog! I'm here to help!

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: Oh, you. You're the girl from the market, aren't you?

items.speaker: Little Lisa
items.text: Yes, that's me.

items.speaker: Little Lisa
items.text: Let's try our best to fix the machine together. But there's no need to worry. Mr. Fog, we can still hold the exhibition even if we can't do it!

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: The exhibition. Alright.

items.speaker: Radio Broadcast
items.text: Next, introducing the London Uluru Exhibition Games.

items.speaker: Radio Broadcast
items.text: So far, 28 players have registered for the six-day event, which will host one sport per day.

items.speaker: Worker I
items.text: Alright, everyone, let's push together! Three, two, one!

items.speaker: Radio Broadcast
items.text: The residents of Cross Street have taken it upon themselves to rebuild the stadium.

items.speaker: Little Lisa
items.text: Hey, your painting's totally off theme. Look, mine's a mockingbird with a gold medal. It just won first place in the singing competition!

items.speaker: Freddy the Rascal
items.text: The Uluru games ain't got a singin' competition. You should've drawn somethin' more athletic, like my sailfish. It's the fastest swimmer in the world.

items.speaker: Radio Broadcast
items.text: How exciting! Our very own Uluru Games without any interference from the Foundation!

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Ms. Tooth Fairy!

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: I've made a list of all the athletes who signed up for the qualifiers. A lot of them have left, but some would like to stay for our exhibition.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: Good. And I've made a list of the daily attendees based on the tickets they bought for the qualifiers.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: Mr. Fog and Mr. Brimley are discussing the possible security issues of the event with the Relief Centre staff and the police.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: We may actually start the Games on the day the qualifiers were originally scheduled.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: But, since this is all improvised, we'll probably encounter some unexpected problems as the Games continue. We need to be prepared.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Yeah, I know.
The girl's enthusiasm dims as she looks over the sports venue, eyes tinged with quiet regret.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: *sigh*

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: Thank you, Flutterpage. It must have taken a lot of effort to make the athlete list. You've done an excellent job.
She continues to scan the venue, as if searching for something.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: So, you saw the whole athlete list. Did you see the name you were hoping for?

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Ah! How did you ...

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Ms. Tooth Fairy, I ...
She hesitates, her brow furrowed. Her lips are barely moving.

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: Flutterpage! Flutterpage!

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: Come here. We need you to explain to the Relief Centre how your little sheets work!
The girl hesitates as she looks toward the somber officials.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: Just go. They need you more than I do. Your explanation may decide whether the Games can be held.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Alright. I'll talk to you later!
She skips excitedly toward the door of the venue, where Brimley and Mr. Fog await her arrival.
As a worker carrying a wooden frame passes, she disappears from view.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: You've got yourself a new outfit. It looks great on you.
A tall, slim woman emerges from the shadows, her pointed leather shoes gliding along the floor with poised restraint.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Oh, I like your coat, too.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: Thank you.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: My grandmother had one just like it. She died two years ago, had a proper sweet tooth, too.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: We'd have got along well.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: How did you know I was here?

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: Oh, I didn't until my toothfairies found you.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Heh. So you have a whole jar of scapegoats who can take all the blame for you? How convenient.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: You've pulled yourself together, haven't you? Even your sarcasm has become bitter again.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: So, why are you here?

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Just getting some fresh air.
The two of them remain silent as they observe the mayhem of the sports ground, workers shouting and children running back and forth.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: Look at them. They're all so happy. What do you think?

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: I've never seen such a rudimentary, disorderly, and poorly prepared event in my life.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: Well of course, it's totally amateur.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: But it's built on enthusiasm and sportsmanship.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: Athletes will go head-to-head, spectators will cheer, and the stadium will be lit up by the energy they release together.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: It's imperfect, yes, but it's inclusive and unstoppable. And that's what makes it special.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Hmph.
Willow holds a crumpled registration form in her hand.
